questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is slowing down by turning off the engine.
It is slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
It is not recommended because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows down the motorcycle, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What lane position is best?

options.text: A position that reduces your space cushion and makes you visible.
A position that increases your space cushion and makes you visible.
A position that increases road hazards and lets others pass easily.
A position that reduces road hazards and lets you follow closely behind vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A position that increases your space cushion and makes you visible.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that gives you more space around you and makes you easy to see. This helps you avoid wind, blind spots, and hazards. It also stops others from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: How should a rider sit to best control a motorcycle?

options.text: Using arms to hold their body up.
With knees away from the gas tank.
With feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: With feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Keep your arms slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Gently use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, ease off the throttle and stay straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: What is downshifting also called?
questions.explanation: Downshifting creates an effect like braking. This is why downshifting is also called engine braking.

questions.question: Why should inexperienced riders ride near the front of a group?

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they lead.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in other positions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: In a group, less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders keep a close eye on them.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the total stopping power on a motorcycle.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are usually white with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road rules, like speed limits. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the right portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
As close as possible to the vehicle in front.
Without signaling, so you don't distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. Signal your intention and check for traffic. Pass when safe, then signal and move back when you can.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, even if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles and still do not see them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: When making a turn:

options.text: There is less grip available for braking.
There is more grip available for braking.
Braking works the same as on a straight road.
You should never try to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less grip available for braking.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but you must be very careful. When a motorcycle leans to turn, some grip is used for turning. This means less grip is available for braking.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the rider and lean with the rider. Sit as far forward as you can without crowding the rider. Hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and affects how your motorcycle handles. Your bike will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more space to stop. Ride slower, start braking sooner, leave more space between you and other vehicles, and wait for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. It is recommended for all riders. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that might catch on the motorcycle and must lean with the rider when turning. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: The body eliminates one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.explanation: To find how much alcohol remains, subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing?
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support your ankles.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, you should focus on:

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane beside you as possible. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but focus on seeing the road behind and beside you.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience. Most crashes happen during the day at low speeds.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as you can before impact. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off the seat. Roll the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel just before you hit the object.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders who have ridden their motorcycles for less than six months.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders who have ridden their motorcycles for less than six months.
questions.explanation: Most crashes involve inexperienced riders. Be extra careful when riding a new motorcycle or one you are not familiar with. Most crashes happen to riders with less than six months of experience.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes the wobble worse. Grip the handlebars firmly. Slow down by gradually closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride through a curve?
questions.explanation: Groups should ride in a staggered formation normally. However, switch to single-file when taking curves, turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.
